text:
marie: Heads-up — I've been poking at noisy canary rollbacks. Today a transient spike triggered a full rollback even though the downstream quality test passed within 3 minutes. Thinking we need a 'canary credit' concept so short blips don't auto-evict.
ajay: can you sketch the idea? :+1:
linda: yup curious. we should also consider latency vs accuracy signals separately.
marie: idea sketch: each canary starts with a credit_bucket (units = signal-weighted minutes). Bad signal consumption drains credits, good signal refills slowly. Only when bucket <= 0 do we escalate to rollback. This avoids knee-jerk evictions for short, noisy bursts.
oliver: interesting. Do we tie credits to absolute traffic % or to absolute request count? If low traffic, one bad request shouldn't matter.
marie: bucket is traffic-weighted: credits -= signal_penalty * request_weight. request_weight = request_tokens / expected_tokens. So larger requests consume more.
tim: what signals count? error_rate, regression_score, p99 latency? We need pluggable signal set per route.
marie: yes, config per route. propose default signals: error_rate (5m), regression_score (eval harness), p95_latency (1m). Each signal has penalty and smoothing window.
qa: how do we avoid credit exhaustion during slow ramp? e.g., steady small penalty but no recovery.
marie: recovery rules: small refill per successful minute; also a decay multiplier that reduces penalties over time (backoff). We also cap maximum credits to allow eventual recovery.
ajay: sketch config YAML please — easier to reason with.
marie: ```yaml
canary_credit:
  initial_credits: 300    # units = seconds-equivalent
  max_credits: 1800
  refill_rate: 2         # units/sec when healthy
  signals:
    - name: error_rate
      window: 60
      penalty: 30
      threshold: 0.02
    - name: regression_score
      window: 300
      penalty: 120
      threshold: 0.05
    - name: p95_latency
      window: 60
      penalty: 10
      threshold: 1200  # ms
  request_weighting: tokens
  exhaustion_action: rollback
  soft_action: divert_to_shadow
```
oliver: nice. For exhaustion_action, could we have 'throttle' then 'rollback' chain? e.g., soft degrade before full rollback.
marie: yes make exhaustion_action an ordered list: [throttle, divert_to_shadow, rollback]
tim: operational concerns: this introduces stateful counters per canary instance. Where live state lives?
marie: two choices: centralized controller (single source of truth) or local shim with periodic reconciliation. Prefer hybrid: local fast-path applies credits locally, reconciles with control plane ledger every 30s. That keeps latency low and still debuggable.
ajay: we need consistency semantics. If local says bucket >0 but central says <=0 due to rolled-up metrics, we must prefer central to enforce safety.
marie: agreed: reconciliation must be authoritative. Local control plane can buffer actions but central can override with immediate revocation.
sre-bot: deploybot: canary-credit prototype deployed to test cluster-2 at 1739459900.
nora: in case central becomes unreachable, local should operate in 'fail-open' or 'fail-closed' mode configurable per tenant.
linda: tenants: enterprise customers might want fail-closed; defaults for public-hosted should be fail-open to avoid outages.
qa: how to surface debug info? need per-canary time series: credits, penalties, signals, last_reconcile_ts.
marie: store time series in telemetry with tag canary_id and route. UI: small sparkline and explanation on the rollout page.
ajay: can we incorporate model-based prediction? e.g., predict next-minute penalty and preemptively throttle.
oliver: maybe later. keep MVP rule-based.
marie: rollout controller API change (proto sketch):
```proto
message CanaryCreditConfig {
  int32 initial_credits = 1;
  int32 max_credits = 2;
  repeated SignalConfig signals = 3;
  repeated string exhaustion_actions = 4; // ordered
}
```
marie: also need telemetry contract: credits_gauge, credit_penalty_events, reconciliation_events, exhaustion_count.
tim: how about test harness? need chaos tests that simulate short spikes to ensure credit avoids rollback and long sustained regressions still rollback.
qa: I'll add tests: rapid spike, jittery latency, sustained slow drift. Also test network partition between local shim and control plane.
marie: ops playbook update: when rollback happens due to credit exhaustion, controller should attach blame: which signals consumed how much.
nora: and alerting: only page for exhaustion if exhaustion_action includes rollback or if canary is enterprise fail-closed.
ajay: few more edge cases: multi-variant canaries where variants share a credit pool vs per-variant buckets. Thoughts?
marie: default per-variant, but optional shared_pool for A/B where we want total risk budget shared.
oliver: cost: more metrics, more reconciliation traffic. Should be fine if sampling is tuned.
marie: next steps: I can draft RFC with config schema, controller state machine, reconciliation semantics, telemetry names. Aim for RFC by Friday. Any objections?
linda: none from me. :+1:
ajay: go for it. minor nit: use 'grace_tokens' instead of 'credits' in RFC? feels clearer.
marie: ok will try 'grace_tokens' in text but keep 'canary_credit' in legacy configs for compatibility.
qa: tagging tests: I'll coordinate with marie for harness infra.
marie: thanks — I'll ping after RFC draft. end of thread.
